channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Youth Olympic Games organisers hail Senegal's capability to host major events
item.description: Dakar 2026 is over. Two weeks of competition, thousands of young athletes and a historic first for Africa. The Youth Olympic Games brought the world to Senegal for the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the continent. From record-breaking performances to historic medals for the host nation, Dakar 2026 has been a celebration of sport, youth and cultural exchange. Our correspondent Aminatou Diallo reports from Dakar.

item.title: France and Cambodia share their love for pétanque in Phnom Penh
item.description: Phnom Penh is hosting the 20th Francophonie Summit this Sunday and Monday. French President Emmanuel Macron is attending as part of a 3-day state visit to Cambodia. France and Cambodia's history is deep rooted and complex, but the two countries have one thing in common: a love for pétanque. Story by Caitlin Brown.

item.title: Washington divided over how to deal with fallout from the Nvidia case
item.description: After the fall, the fallout. US government agencies are squabbling after AI leader Jensen Huang stepped down from chips giant Nvidia in disgrace. The Treasury says it wanted to blacklist a Singapore company at the heart of the scandal, but the Commerce Department didn't act. Megaspeed was run by suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who reportedly had an affair with Jensen Huang. Details by Peter O'Brien.

item.title: Man, 21, stabbed to death in London
item.description: Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward after a 21-year-old man died following a stabbing in London.

item.title: FAA blames Friday's ground stop on 'equipment issue' during telecoms network upgrade
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said initial investigations pointed to an issue with contractor L3Harris updating old tech at a remote location. (Image credit: Adam Gray)

item.title: FAA ground stop live updates: 'Zero evidence of anything nefarious,' FAA head says
item.description: The DHS secretary said there were no indications of a cyberattack.

item.title: US: What exactly caused the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years?
item.description: After a nearly five-hour ground stoppage, flights in the US have resumed. However, officials are warning that it will take days to recover from the ongoing delays related to the incident. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy explained the crisis was due to a failure in ageing telecommunications equipment. What exactly happened? Answers with FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Shirli Sitbon.

item.title: US Transport Secretary asks Congress for $30 bn to upgrade aviation infrastructure
item.description: A failure in aging telecommunications equipment Friday forced a nationwide halt to departures from US airports. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says officials have found no evidence so far of a cyberattack, but that they're not ruling it out. Details by Jack Pownall.

item.title: Wales claim historic victory against All Blacks for first time since 1953
item.description: Wales claimed a historic 35-28 victory over New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday, securing their first win over the All Blacks since 1953.

item.title: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's far-right president
item.description: Chile's far-right President José Antonio Kast is facing mounting public anger, as rising fuel prices trigger transport strikes and protests across the country. (Image credit: Esteban Felix)

item.title: Wales beat the All Blacks for first time since 1953
item.description: Wales have beaten New Zealand in a men's rugby union match for the first time in 73 years.

item.title: 'Poisoned chalice': French presidential hopeful Riner rebuffs Macron's backing
item.description: French judo champion Teddy Riner on Saturday publicly distanced himself from President Emmanuel Macron, calling his endorsement a "poisoned chalice". The presidential hopeful seeks to position himself as an alternative to France's political extremes.

item.title: Microsoft confirms all services are restored after global outage
item.description: Microsoft has said that all services have been fully restored after a global outage which affected the NHS, police, schools and other services across the UK.

item.title: DR Congo, Rwanda clash over Francophonie leadership as Macron seeks compromise
item.description: DR Congo and Rwanda clashed Saturday over the leadership of the Francophonie, as tensions between the neighbouring countries spilled into the race to head the 53-member organisation. French President Emmanuel Macron urged Rwanda to withdraw its candidate in favour of a compromise choice ahead of Monday's vote.

item.title: Former SAS chief blames state for breaking 'moral contract' with soldiers
item.description: A former commanding officer of the SAS blamed the state for breaking a "moral contract" between the country and its top soldiers by setting up an inquiry into war crimes which has failed to reach conclusions four years on.

item.title: 'I never imagined my father was a Nazi': Born in a German-run 'baby factory'
item.description: Two trainloads of children, some of them born in Nazi-run "Lebensborn" maternity homes, were brought from Germany to Commercy in eastern France in 1946. One of those on board was Édith Pagot.

item.title: USA: All passengers survive after tanker hits docked river cruise ship in New Orleans
item.description: A portion of the Mississippi River remains closed after a collision between an oil tanker and a riverboat forced a chaotic river rescue in Louisiana. Story by Caitlin Brown.

item.title: US asked if Ukraine would give up parts of Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
item.description: The US has asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region if Kyiv were admitted to NATO, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

item.title: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
item.description: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly. (Image credit: Lindsey Wasson)

item.title: Perspective: A new kind of White House press secretary
item.description: With the White House press secretary job still left unfilled, maybe an AI assistant might be the answer? (Image credit: Alex Brandon)

item.title: Inside Ethiopia's war: Rare access to a hospital treating victims of renewed fighting
item.description: Ethiopia's renewed conflict is taking an increasing toll on civilians, with humanitarian organisations reporting a rise in casualties. In the Amhara region, FRANCE 24’s correspondent Tom Canetti was granted rare access to a civilian hospital where surgeons are struggling to treat the influx of wounded patients. But for many caught in the fighting, reaching medical care is a challenge in itself. Warning: The report contains images of surgery that may be confronting for some viewers.

item.title: Who are the 'street medics' showing up at protests around the world?
item.description: From treating tear gas exposure to tending to injuries, street medics have become an increasingly common sight at protests all over the world. But who exactly are they and when did they start showing up at demonstrations? Story by Daniel Quinlan.

item.title: U2 releases first new studio album in a decade, 'Caranaval de Luz'
item.description: U2 just released a new album after nine years of no new content. And fans are already rocking out to the new songs. Details on the Irish rock band’s comeback by Ophelie Jacobson.

item.title: Half a million people gather for an open-air mass by Pope Leo in Peru
item.description: Pope Leo said it was a "joy to be back" in his second home of Chiclayo, where he made his name as a bishop. This is the latest stop on his South America tour, the very tour that saw fears of cancellation after the Pope underwent surgery for lung cancer. Story by Vedika Bahl.

item.title: Microsoft's widespread outages caused global chaos, including in the healthcasre industry
item.description: Microsoft says it is seeing improvements in its service availability after an hours-long disruption knocked out its platforms including Outlook and Teams. The outage has affected hundreds of millions of people across the globe. The healthcare industry was among those impacted, as Ophelie Jacobson explains.

item.title: France fend off South African comeback to clinch long-awaited win in Paris
item.description: Twenty-one years after last beating the Springboks in Paris, Les Bleus held out for a 21-19 win over the world champions on Friday after a nailbiting finale. Antoine Dupont and company are now one step away from reaching the Nations Championship final in London.

item.title: US proposed Ukraine cedes Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, Zelensky says
item.description: President Zelensky said the US had proposed ceding Ukraine's eastern city of Donbas to Russia, in exchange for Ukrainian membership of NATO, following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi this week. He reiterated that Kyiv was not willing to retreat from its territory and warned that the Kremlin's bid to change the continent's security architecture could lead to more wars.

item.title: 'Climate action is alive': Triumphant Democrats attend COP31 summit shunned by Trump
item.description: A delegation of 18 Democratic lawmakers arrived at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Saturday to reaffirm the US commitment to tackling global warming following their sweeping midterm election victory.

item.title: SpaceX's Starship encounters problems during 15th test flight
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX successfully launched its Starship, the world's largest spaceship, into orbit where it should release 15 satellites for its Starlink network. A few minutes after lift off however, the rocket's booster which was meant to return to the pad splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico. Details by Daniel Quinlan.

item.title: Can Nvidia survive without tech titan Jensen Huang?
item.description: The Financial Times says computing giant Nvidia has approached Rene Haas, CEO of British chip designer Arm, in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. Huang resigned after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Meanwhile some employees are clamouring for Huang's return – as his fellow tech leader Elon Musk. A sign of Huang's lingering star power, in an industry where so often the fate of each giant company depends on one man. Story by Peter O'Brien.

item.title: France's school principals say threats and violence have become unbearable
item.description: Headteachers gathered across France this Friday, to demonstrate their frustration after nearly two months of student protests that have blockaded high schools. Many of the teachers support the students, but say they feel exhausted and isolated as the violence has surged. They are calling the government to protect them. Story by Vedika Bahl.

item.title: France protests for fifth Saturday against living costs and heavy-handed policing
item.description: Different causes are set to come together for one march in Paris this Saturday. Campaign groups, students and Yellow Vest protesters are due to join forces in the capital, bringing together demands on wages, education and civil liberties. But after weeks of demonstrations, union leaders warn that protest fatigue is setting in, while police officers are seeking better compensation for the risk of policing the protests. Story by Jack Pownall.

item.title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
item.description: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001. Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed.

item.title: Business secretary to hold further talks with Poundland owners amid rescue talks
item.description: Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, is to hold further talks with Poundland's owner and its management team amid a race to save the discount retailer from collapse.

item.title: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
item.description: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump. (Image credit: Brandon Bell)

item.title: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
item.description: Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests. (Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
item.description: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions. (Image credit: Olga Pankova)

item.title: 2 Americans die in suspected drowning incident in the Bahamas
item.description: Two Americans died in a suspected drowning incident in the Bahamas on Friday afternoon after a group of swimmers was swept away by strong currents, police said.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold unprecedented meeting, White House says
item.description: The leaders of the US, China and Russia will hold an unprecedented meeting on the sidelines of a major economic summit, the White House has said.

item.title: Goalkeeper given 12-game ban for fatal collision with Tenerife striker
item.description: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 games after an on-field collision that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

item.title: Live: More than 100,000 protest across France, interior ministry says
item.description: Around 106,000 people took to the streets across France on Saturday, including 24,000 in Paris, according to the interior ministry. Some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes were deployed nationwide to oversee between 50 and 60 planned marches. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Murder investigation launched after 'shocking attack by men in balaclavas'
item.description: A 27-year-old man was stabbed to death in a north Manchester suburb in the early hours of Saturday morning.

item.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
item.description: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history. (Image credit: Eric Stone)

item.title: Trump to meet with Putin and Xi in China next week, US officials say
item.description: Trump will participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China, and Russia on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in China next week.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
item.description: Supporters and donors have been encouraging GOP Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, sources told ABC News.

item.title: Schumer and Van Hollen face off for Senate majority leader. What do Democrats think?
item.description: Within moments of Chris Van Hollen announcing his intent to challenge Chuck Schumer in a race to lead next year’s Senate Democratic majority, endorsements began flying.

item.description: British representatives will be part of a team representing Europe in Ukraine peace talks.

item.title: WATCH: 41-year-old firefighter’s life saved by heart transplant
item.description: Nico Ratto, a dad of two from New Jersey, spent 45 days hospitalized before receiving a lifesaving heart transplant.

item.title: WATCH: Heartwarming update on Punch the Monkey
item.description: The baby macaque at Japan’s Ichikawa City Zoo became a viral sensation after turning to an IKEA toy for comfort. Nine months later, Punch has joined the troop and taken an interest in a baby macaque.

item.description: The daredevil couple who were arrested after climbing to the top of the Empire State Building were in court on Thursday to face criminal charges and possible deportation.

item.description: Maryland Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge New York Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader in the new Congress.

item.title: WATCH: School's ultimate class trip heads to Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New reports on a group of middle schoolers in Maryland who are about to get the snow day of their lives in the form of a class trip to Antarctica.

item.description: A tanker truck driver managed to escape from his vehicle just seconds before a train slammed into his truck.

item.description: US officer who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia is 41-year-old Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, according to a source familiar with the investigation.

item.description: The question is whether his victory can establish a lasting realignment.

item.description: The airline says customers who give their personal and credit card information to AI businesses run the risk of having their sensitive data exposed.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, health ministry says
item.description: An Israeli airstrike on a Palestinian hospital has killed at least six and wounded 28, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.

item.description: President Donald Trump spoke at a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery honoring fallen soldiers and addressed the war with Iran.

item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.

item.description: On Veterans Day, ABC News' Danny New talks to two cheerleaders for the Philadelphia Eagles who've also served their country.
